nationalDesk.title: FAA nationwide ground stop
nationalDesk.summary: Nov 13: FAA grounded all U.S. flights ~3:30-8:15 PM ET; legacy network overwhelmed by data; FAA sees no cyberattack.
nationalDesk.angle: Everybody wants the system modernized; nobody wants it down for the upgrade.
nationalDesk.valley: HRL, MFE and BRO issued advisories; Brownsville still had 5 cancellations that night.
nationalDesk.detail: FAA: legacy equipment became unstable when data flooded its FTI network; suspected sites a radar site in Amarillo and a radio site in El Dorado, AR where L3Harris was deploying a router; 17 of 22 en route centers affected; ~3,500 aircraft landed safely; ~12,462 flights canceled that day. Second nationwide ground stop since 9/11 (ABC). FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told Congress Nov 18: 'blame me.' Duffy said the issue came on the 69th router installation. Harlingen: incoming banks from IAH/DFW/AUS couldn't depart. No current FAA flight cuts found in the sources checked.

nationalDesk.title: Mullin testifies on outages and the LSU-Texas flight
nationalDesk.summary: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin told House Homeland Security (Nov 18) the outages weren't a coordinated attack; defended flying to the LSU-Texas game.
nationalDesk.angle: Fair question or cheap shot? The optics of flying to a game during a grounding are rough.
nationalDesk.valley: DHS runs the border; ask what RGV ranchers, bridges and Border Patrol are actually seeing.
nationalDesk.detail: Hearing: 'Worldwide Threats to the Homeland: 25 Years After 9/11,' with DNI Jay Clayton and FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia. Clayton: 'separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes,' not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack. Mullin said he wanted to be a good uncle and will reimburse the government; he was also pressed on ICE training. His written testimony says Southwest border apprehensions fell 58% in FY2026 (DHS's claim).

nationalDesk.title: SNL: Mulaney, Bridgers and the 'Sister' sketch
nationalDesk.summary: Nov 14: John Mulaney hosted (7th time), Phoebe Bridgers sang; 'CIA Meeting' cold open roasted tech CEOs; critics called it the season's best.
nationalDesk.angle: A cold open that skips politics and still lands. 'Sister' hit people in the gut.
nationalDesk.valley: The cold open roasted the same ground stop that sent HRL, MFE and BRO advisories.
nationalDesk.detail: Cold open: Mulaney as a CIA officer lecturing Musk, Altman, Thiel, Zuckerberg and Amodei about honey-trap spies after the Jensen Huang scandal; Bowen Yang returned as Huang. Also: 'Sister,' 'Plane Crash,' 'Gettin' It Done,' 'Woodstock,' 'Kathy,' and a Central Park carriage ride musical sketch. Bridgers: 'Bobby' and 'Still Standing.' Reaction: EW 'easily the best episode of this season'; Boston.com 'far and away the best'; ratings 4.45M, down 20% from the prior week (Showbiz411). The 'Sister' video: a pretaped fake elder-care testimonial ad (Jane Wickline as the sister), SNL's YouTube channel, published Nov 14, 2:59, ~5.8M views when checked Nov 18. Last new episode before Thanksgiving; next is in December (Amanda Seyfried, per EW).

nationalDesk.title: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns
nationalDesk.summary: Nov 12: Nvidia said Huang resigned as CEO and board member effective immediately; CFO Colette Kress is interim CEO.
nationalDesk.angle: The AI boom's biggest face is gone, and Nvidia chips still power every data center.
nationalDesk.valley: Starbase's $24B data center is exactly that kind of AI compute fight.
nationalDesk.detail: Source for the resignation facts is Nvidia's own press release. Mainstream reports link it to an alleged affair with a suspected Chinese spy (the SNL cold open built on it); verify allegation details through a reported source before characterizing them.

nationalDesk.title: Texas Ten Commandments law in doubt
nationalDesk.summary: ABC (Nov 18): Democratic midterm wins put Texas's classroom Ten Commandments mandate in doubt; the law still stands.
nationalDesk.angle: Whatever you think of it, parents deserve a straight answer on what's on the classroom wall.
nationalDesk.valley: It applies in every RGV school; ask what your child's classroom has up.
nationalDesk.detail: ABC reports legal battles over classroom displays are headed toward the Supreme Court. The law remains in effect unless courts or lawmakers change it. Verify details of repeal efforts before airing.

items.title: Roblox: 'Steal An Egg' & 'Throw Food For Animals'
items.what: Steal An Egg is Roblox's #1 game (about 1.17M playing); Throw Food For Animals is #2 and up 58% on the week.
items.means: Pet-collecting games where other players can take your eggs; paid boosts are optional.
items.tip: Ask 'who's stealing your eggs?' Set chat to friends-only and a spending limit.
items.pwhat: Roblox's #1 game: pet-collecting 'Steal An Egg' (1.17M playing); other players can grab your eggs.
items.ptip: Ask 'who's stealing your eggs?' Friends-only chat, spending limit.

items.what: A catchphrase kids yell for laughs, often with a hands-weighing gesture.
items.means: No fixed meaning; some link it to LaMelo Ball (6'7"). Already being mocked as overused.
items.tip: Laugh and ask them to show you the gesture; it's meant to confuse adults.

items.tip: Ask 'would you laugh if that was your cousin?' It's a natural bridge to the bullying talk.

items.title: The Door Kick Challenge
items.what: A TikTok trend: kick or pound a stranger's front door, film it, run.
items.means: Police say it can mean vandalism, trespass or burglary charges, and a scared homeowner may react.
items.tip: It's a crime, not a prank; Irvine PD says parents can be held accountable. Ask what they'd do if friends filmed it.

items.title: Slang: aura, aura farming, cooked
items.what: 'Aura' = someone's vibe; 'aura farming' = doing things to look cool online; 'cooked' = in trouble.
items.means: Words to question: 'huzz,' 'bop,' 'big back' can objectify or mock women and bodies.
items.tip: Be curious, not corrective: ask what a word means. Terms burn out fast.
